stops.title: How he marks
stops.note: How he marks, the answer formula and a 60-minute plan. Read it once.

stops.title: Q1 Tool error: what do you do next?
stops.note: A tool error and four moves. Try his question first, then read why.

stops.title: Q2 Is it a refactoring?
stops.note: Behaviour stays the same and the tests still pass. That is the whole test.

stops.title: Q3 A mypy error: which fix?
stops.note: One mypy error and the fix that removes the cause, not the warning.

stops.title: Q4 A test fails: what can you conclude?
stops.note: A failing test says the test and the code disagree. It does not say which one is wrong.

stops.title: Q5 Name the clean-code problem
stops.note: A function with several jobs. Name the problem and what a teammate cannot do.

stops.title: Q6 What does this command print?
stops.note: Read a pipe and say what it prints. Count lines, not words.

stops.title: Q7 Read code and say what is wrong (open)
stops.note: Open: say what the code does, name two problems, say how you would change it.

stops.title: Q8 Compare a diff and two commit messages (open)
stops.note: Open: say what the diff does, pick the better message, name one test in words.

stops.title: Q9 Read tool output (open, harder)
stops.note: Open: sort the mypy errors, say which one crashes, answer the `# type: ignore` question.

stops.title: Break
